_comment: Maps Lab Mode scenarios and Protocol Viz protocols to CompTIA Network+ / CCNA exam objectives.

objectives: N10-009 2.1 — Compare and contrast OSI model layers
N10-009 2.3 — Explain the role of ARP in IPv4 communications
CCNA 2.7 — Configure and verify Layer 2 discovery protocols
Find the Rogue Device.study_note: ARP scanning is the primary technique for discovering Layer 2 devices. A device that appears in ARP replies but not in DHCP leases is a candidate rogue device.

objectives: N10-009 1.5 — Explain DNS record types and resolution
N10-009 3.3 — Use appropriate tools to troubleshoot DNS issues
CCNA 1.6 — Configure and verify DNS
Diagnose Slow DNS.study_note: Slow DNS resolution is often mistaken for a general connectivity problem. Measuring DNS latency separately from ping RTT isolates whether the resolver or the network path is at fault.

objectives: N10-009 2.2 — Spanning Tree Protocol and loop prevention
CCNA 2.5 — Configure and verify STP (802.1D, RSTP)
Identify the Broadcast Storm Source.study_note: STP prevents Layer 2 broadcast storms by electing a root bridge and placing redundant ports into blocking state. RSTP (802.1w) provides faster convergence.

objectives: N10-009 1.4 — Given a scenario, apply concepts of IP addressing and subnetting
N10-009 2.1 — Compare and contrast OSI model layers
Map Your Subnet.study_note: A subnet map is the foundation of every troubleshooting session — knowing which addresses are gateway, DHCP pool, and static assignments makes every later diagnosis faster.

objectives: N10-009 1.5 — Explain DNS record types and resolution
N10-009 3.3 — Use appropriate tools to troubleshoot DNS issues
CCNA 1.6 — Configure and verify DNS
Measure Your DNS Resolver Speed.study_note: DNS resolver latency directly impacts application response time. Anything above 100 ms for a local resolver or 200 ms for a public resolver warrants investigation.

objectives: N10-009 1.4 — Explain common TCP/IP protocols and their port numbers
N10-009 4.2 — Compare and contrast network attacks (port scanning)
CCNA 5.2 — Configure and verify access control lists
Find an Open Port.study_note: A port scan enumerates listening services. Open ports represent potential attack surface — every open port should have a documented business reason.

objectives: N10-009 1.5 — Explain the function of DHCP (DORA process)
N10-009 3.3 — Troubleshoot IP address assignment issues
CCNA 1.6 — Configure and verify DHCP client and relay
Detect a DHCP Conflict.study_note: Two DHCP servers on the same broadcast domain create IP conflicts. The DORA sequence (Discover → Offer → Request → Acknowledge) is a core exam topic.

objectives: N10-009 3.1 — Explain network performance metrics (latency, jitter, loss)
N10-009 3.3 — Use appropriate tools to measure network performance
Measure Network Jitter.study_note: Jitter is the variation in packet arrival times. High jitter (>30 ms) degrades real-time traffic such as VoIP and video calls even when average latency is acceptable.

objectives: N10-009 2.1 — Explain the purpose and function of MAC addresses
N10-009 2.3 — Explain the role of the OUI in MAC address allocation
Identify Device Manufacturers.study_note: The first 24 bits of a MAC address (OUI — Organisationally Unique Identifier) identify the manufacturer. This is used in asset management and anomaly detection.

objectives: N10-009 1.2 — Explain network topologies (star, mesh, ring, bus)
N10-009 1.3 — Summarise cloud concepts and connectivity
CCNA 1.1 — Explain the role of network components
Read a Network Topology Map.study_note: Topology maps show the logical and physical relationships between network nodes. Being able to read and draw these diagrams is tested in both exams.

objectives: N10-009 2.3 — Explain the role of ARP
CCNA 2.7 — ARP and Layer 2 address resolution
ARP.study_note: ARP resolves IPv4 addresses to MAC addresses within a broadcast domain. ARP spoofing (man-in-the-middle) is a common Layer 2 attack covered in Security+.

objectives: N10-009 1.5 — DNS record types and resolution process
CCNA 1.6 — DNS operation and configuration
DNS.study_note: DNS uses UDP port 53 for queries and TCP port 53 for zone transfers. Recursive and iterative resolution are both exam topics.

objectives: N10-009 1.4 — TCP vs UDP: connection-oriented vs connectionless
CCNA 1.5 — TCP three-way handshake and connection termination
TCP.study_note: SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK is the TCP three-way handshake. Connection teardown uses FIN/FIN-ACK/ACK. Understanding sequence/acknowledgement numbers is essential.

objectives: N10-009 1.5 — DHCP DORA process
CCNA 1.6 — DHCP client, server and relay agent
DHCP.study_note: DHCP uses UDP ports 67 (server) and 68 (client). The DORA sequence (Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge) is used to assign IP addresses dynamically.

objectives: N10-009 2.2 — Spanning Tree Protocol and loop prevention
CCNA 2.5 — Configure and verify STP (802.1D, RSTP)
STP.study_note: STP prevents Layer 2 broadcast storms by electing a root bridge and placing redundant ports into blocking state. RSTP (802.1w) provides faster convergence.

objectives: N10-009 4.2 — Identify common network attacks
N10-009 3.3 — Use appropriate tools for network troubleshooting
SY0-701 1.2 — Summarise vulnerability scanning concepts
SY0-701 4.3 — Implement vulnerability management activities
